title: 万事俱备只欠客  (Windproof and Ready)

segments.t: Late Saturday morning arrives bright and breezy at Courtyard Inn. At five minutes to twelve, Qing, Mei, and Hao stand under the courtyard tree admiring twenty-four coral-and-gold lanterns swaying steadily from the upper balcony down to the branches. Listen first.
抬头看阳台拉下来的那四条绳——过了一整夜，一盏灯笼都没拧歪！
再低头看餐桌：二十八条亚麻餐巾全被编好号的桦木夹咬得死死的！
老陈甚至给每块白桌布的四个角也多夹了四个木衣夹！
下午三点我烤四个莓果杏仁蛋糕，到六点端出来正好温热。
下午四点我和宋老师把四手联弹钢琴曲最后排练一遍！
每件事都掐表算准了：下午备菜，五点半沏茶，六点整开迎！
小晴，快敲敲木头！谁要是敢说分秒不差，准得出点儿岔子！
大中午的能有什么变故？人家客人可是用黑墨水白纸黑字写明今晚六点呀！
等等——你们俩听见透过大堂窗户传过来的前台电话铃声了吗？
小晴，这星期六中午的电话铃响得又响又急呀！
连玻璃门后的老陈都刚从纸账本上抬起头了！
帮我拿一下围裙——趁十二点钟声还没敲完，我得赶紧接电话！
Now let's go through it line by line with the English translation.
抬头看阳台拉下来的那四条绳——过了一整夜，一盏灯笼都没拧歪！

'Look up at those four lines from the balcony—after a whole night, not one lantern twisted!' Mei says "yi zheng ye" for the entire night from dusk to dawn, and "ningwai" describes a cord twisting crookedly.
再低头看餐桌：二十八条亚麻餐巾全被编好号的桦木夹咬得死死的！

'And look down at the tables: all twenty-eight linen napkins are clamped tight by numbered birch pins!' "Bianhao" means assigned a number ("bianhao de"), while vivid "yaode sisi de" jokes that the wooden clips are "biting down hard" on the cloth.
老陈甚至给每块白桌布的四个角也多夹了四个木衣夹！

'Chen even clipped four extra wooden clothespins onto the corners of every white tablecloth!' Flat cloth sheets use the counter "kuai" ("mei kuai bai zhuobu"), and "shenzhi" highlights that Chen went even further.
下午三点我烤四个莓果杏仁蛋糕，到六点端出来正好温热。

'At three this afternoon I'll bake four berry almond cakes so they're nice and warm by six.' "Wenre" captures that pleasant "warm, not scorching" temperature ideal for fresh cake, timed right for "liu dian" (six o'clock).
下午四点我和宋老师把四手联弹钢琴曲最后排练一遍！

'And at four this afternoon Song and I run through our four-hand piano duet one last time!' "Sishou liandan" is the crisp musical expression for two pianists sharing one keyboard ("four hands linked playing").
每件事都掐表算准了：下午备菜，五点半沏茶，六点整开迎！

'Everything is timed down to the minute: afternoon prep, five-thirty tea, six sharp welcome!' Idiom "qiabiao suanzhun" literally means "pinch a stopwatch and calculate accurately," while "liu dian zheng" stresses six on the dot.
小晴，快敲敲木头！谁要是敢说分秒不差，准得出点儿岔子！

'Knock on wood right now, Qing! Whenever someone boasts down to the second, a hitch is bound to pop up!' "Fenmiao bucha" means "not off by a minute or second," and playful "chazi" refers to an unexpected snag or hiccup.
大中午的能有什么变故？人家客人可是用黑墨水白纸黑字写明今晚六点呀！

'What could possibly change at noon? Our guest wrote six tonight in black ink on white paper!' "Baizhi heizi" ("white paper, black characters") means written down unmistakably in black and white, and "biangu" means a sudden twist.
等等——你们俩听见透过大堂窗户传过来的前台电话铃声了吗？

'Wait—do you two hear the front-desk telephone ringing through the lobby window?' "Touguo ... chuan guolai" traces sound carrying right through ("touguo") the window glass, and "lingsheng" means the ringtone.
小晴，这星期六中午的电话铃响得又响又急呀！
'That's a mighty loud, mighty urgent Saturday noon ring, Qing!' Doubling "you" in "you xiang you ji" literally links two traits at once: both loud and urgent.
连玻璃门后的老陈都刚从纸账本上抬起头了！
'Even Chen behind the glass door just looked up from his paper ledger!' Hao uses "taiqi" (lift up) with "tou" (head) for looking up, while "lian ... dou" underscores how unusual the ring is.
帮我拿一下围裙——趁十二点钟声还没敲完，我得赶紧接电话！

'Hold my apron a second—I'd better answer that call before all twelve noon chimes finish!' Qing pairs "chen" with "hai mei" (literally "while not yet") to urge answering before the chimes end, and "ganjin" adds speed.

Every lantern and clothespin is ready for six this evening—until a noon telephone call flips the Saturday schedule upside down! End of Episode Four—see you in Episode Five!
